specs.title: Export reports as CSV
sources: Owner request: let users export reports as CSV
Current reports page: table with columns Date, Region, Orders, Revenue; users filter by date range
in_scope: A CSV export action on the reports page
The file carries the four table columns in the table's order
non_goals: Changes to the on-page table, its columns or its date filter

criteria.text: Given the reports page shows a table, when the user chooses export as CSV, then the file has a header row Date, Region, Orders, Revenue and one line per exported row, as open question 1 defines the rows
criteria.check: Integration test: export a fixture report, parse the file, compare header and rows with the fixture.

criteria.text: Given a date range is set on the filter, when the user exports, then the file contains only rows whose date is inside that range, including both boundary dates
criteria.check: Integration test with fixed dates at both boundaries.

criteria.text: Given an end date earlier than the start date, when the user exports, then no file is produced and the user sees an error
criteria.check: Negative test: submit the invalid range and assert no download and an error message.

expected_areas: Data access behind the reports page

open_questions.question: Does the export contain only the filtered rows, or all rows of the report?

options.changes: Matches what the user sees; criteria 1 and 2 apply as written
Criterion 2 is removed; files are larger and may not match the screen

open_questions.question: What does the export contain when the filter matches no rows?

options.changes: Users get a valid, empty file

options.option: No file, with a message that nothing matched
options.changes: Users see why there is no file; criterion 1 gets an extra case

open_questions.question: What encoding, delimiter and date format does the file use?

options.option: UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, comma delimiter, ISO dates
options.changes: Hebrew and Russian text opens correctly in common spreadsheet tools

options.option: Another encoding, delimiter or date format
options.changes: Changes how the file opens in spreadsheet tools and what criterion 1 checks

open_questions.question: Is there a maximum number of rows per export?

options.changes: Very large exports stay possible and may time out

options.option: A stated limit with a message when it is reached
options.changes: Adds a failure criterion; see the separate question on large exports in the CSV export line

actions_now: Writes a draft spec with three criteria that no open question blocks and four open questions for the owner. Nothing is approved; the implementer waits for the owner's answers before building the blocked criteria.

specs.title: Discount at checkout
sources: Owner request: add a discount to checkout
Binding: no provisional choices for prices
in_scope: A discount line shown in the checkout total
The total after discount is the sum of the items minus the discount
non_goals: Other offers, promotions or price changes outside checkout

criteria.text: Given a checkout with a discount applied, when the total is shown, then the discount appears as its own line and the total equals the item sum minus the discount
criteria.check: Test: compute totals for fixture carts with and without a discount and compare.

criteria.text: Given a checkout without any discount, when the total is shown, then no discount line appears and the total is unchanged from today
criteria.check: Regression test against the current checkout totals.

open_questions.question: How large is the discount, and is it a percentage or a fixed amount?

options.option: A fixed percentage set by the owner
options.changes: Criterion 3 states the percentage; the calculation rounds per the chosen rule
Criterion 3 states the amount; small carts can go below zero, needing a floor rule

open_questions.question: Who gets the discount?

options.changes: No eligibility criterion
Adds an eligibility criterion and a not-eligible failure path

open_questions.question: Does the discount combine with other offers?

options.option: No, only one offer per order
options.changes: Adds a criterion that a second offer is refused
Adds a criterion for the order of application and the result

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version, draft. Criteria 1 and 2 do not depend on the open questions; criterion 3 waits for them.

actions_now: Writes a draft spec with the two criteria that do not depend on price decisions and three open questions for the owner on size, eligibility and combination. The price decisions are escalated; nothing is chosen for the owner.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec CSV export version 1, approved by the owner (dl-014)
Implementer report: the reports API returns no customer emails, and adding them is outside this line
non_goals: Customer email addresses in the export, unless the owner brings them into a line that changes the reports API

criteria.text: Withdrawn in version 2: criterion 3 of version 1 (the export includes the customer's email) is removed from this line
criteria.check: None: the criterion is withdrawn, so no check applies in this line.

open_questions.question: Should the customer's email be in the export, and if so, in which line?

options.option: Leave it out of CSV export; a separate line adds it to the reports API first
options.changes: Export stays inside this line's scope; the API line is planned separately

options.option: Add it inside this line, extending the reports API
options.changes: Widens this line into the API, which the implementer reports is outside it; needs a new line

versions: 1 (2026-11-27 or earlier): approved by the owner (dl-014).

2 (2026-11-27): withdraws criterion 3, which the reports API cannot yet satisfy; numbers of the other criteria are kept. Draft until the owner approves version 2; work built against version 1 is checked against this version.

actions_now: Issues version 2 as a draft that withdraws criterion 3 and leaves version 1 unchanged, and asks the owner to approve it and decide where customer email belongs. The implementer continues with the other criteria.

specs.title: Dashboard load time
sources: Owner request: make the dashboard faster
Dashboard has three views: Overview, Sales, Inventory
in_scope: Time to a usable dashboard on each of the three views
non_goals: Changes to what the views show or to the data they show

criteria.text: Given each of the Overview, Sales and Inventory views loaded under the reference conditions in open question 1, when the load is measured, then the measured value meets the target in open question 2
criteria.check: Performance test against a baseline measured on the current code under the same reference conditions.

expected_areas: Dashboard views and the data they request

open_questions.question: How is speed measured: which metric, reference data and device?

options.option: Time to first usable render, 75th percentile, on a fixed dataset
options.changes: Measures what the user sees; needs a fixed dataset
Ignores rendering; does not show what the user feels

open_questions.question: What is fast enough for each view?

options.option: A fixed time per view, set after a baseline measurement
options.changes: Criterion 1 gets a number per view

options.option: A percentage reduction from the baseline
options.changes: Criterion 1 becomes relative; the target depends on the baseline run

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version, draft. No target is set until the owner answers the open questions.

actions_now: Writes a draft spec whose one criterion waits for the owner's measurement and target. The current baseline for the three views can be measured now as input to the owner's decision, without setting a target.

specs.title: Settings kept across devices
sources: Owner request: users keep their settings across devices, with theme and language
The owner named a table; the spec states behaviour only, and the architect chooses the storage
in_scope: Theme and language choices of each user
The same choices on every device where the user signs in
non_goals: Settings other than theme and language, until the owner answers open question 1
The storage design, which belongs to the architect

criteria.text: Given a user changes the theme to a supported value on one device, when the user signs in on another device, then that device shows the same theme
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of one user.

criteria.text: Given a user changes the language, when the user signs in on another device, then that device shows the same language
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of one user.

criteria.text: Given a user who has never changed a setting, when the user signs in on any device, then the app shows its current default theme and language
criteria.check: Test against the current defaults with a new account on two devices.

criteria.text: Given a user submits a value that is not supported, when the change is saved, then it is refused, an error is shown and the previous value is kept
criteria.check: Negative test with an unsupported value.

open_questions.question: Are theme and language the only settings to keep across devices?

options.changes: Scope stays as written

options.option: Other settings too, named by the owner
options.changes: Adds criteria for each named setting

open_questions.question: Which theme values are supported?

options.changes: Criterion 1 checks these two values
Criterion 1 covers the third value; criterion 3 needs a default

open_questions.question: What happens when the same setting changes on two devices while one is offline?

options.changes: Adds a criterion that the latest change is the one shown
Different rule; criterion 1 would not hold as written

actions_now: Writes a draft spec that describes the behaviour of theme and language across devices, leaves the table design to the architect, and asks the owner three questions on scope, supported values and conflicts.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: Dark mode spec, version 1, as drafted by the product role
Coordinating session's provisional approval, recorded in the decision queue as waiting for the owner
in_scope: Dark mode for the app's screens, switched by the settings toggle
non_goals: Email templates and the printable invoice view, which stay light under the provisional choice in open question 1

criteria.text: Given the user switches dark mode on in settings, when any main screen is opened, then the screen shows dark mode
criteria.check: End-to-end test over each main screen.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is off, when any main screen is opened, then the screen shows light mode
criteria.check: End-to-end test over each main screen.

expected_areas: Shared styling of the app's screens

open_questions.question: Do email templates and the printable invoice view follow the dark mode toggle?

options.option: No, they stay light (provisional choice, recorded in the queue)
options.changes: Matches the non-goal above; no criteria for them
Adds criteria for both; the printable invoice may need a separate light style

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version, draft. Status changed to approved-provisional by the coordinating session while the owner is away; the decision queue entry waits for the owner. This is a provisional approval, not the owner's approval, and the owner's decision is not yet recorded.

actions_now: Adds the scope question on email templates and the invoice view to the spec, with the provisional choice that they stay light, and records the spec as approved-provisional as the coordinating session has done; the owner's confirmation waits in the decision queue.

specs.title: Password reset
sources: Product role's spec Password reset, version 1
Binding: the owner approves specs
in_scope: Requesting a reset link by email
Setting a new password from the link
non_goals: Changes to sign-in or to account creation

criteria.text: Given a registered email address, when a reset is requested, then an email with a single-use link is sent
criteria.check: Integration test with a mail stub.

criteria.text: Given a reset link that has expired, when it is opened, then the user sees an error and can request a new link
criteria.check: Integration test with a mocked clock.

criteria.text: Given an email address that is not registered, when a reset is requested, then the response is the same as for a registered address and no email is sent
criteria.check: Negative test comparing the two responses.

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version, draft. Waiting for the owner's approval.

actions_now: Presents the draft spec to the owner in chat and asks for approval. The product role does not approve it; the implementer waits for the owner's approval before starting.

specs.title: Dark mode toggle in settings
sources: Owner request: dark mode as a toggle on the settings page that applies to the whole app
Current app: email template system and printable invoice view exist
in_scope: The toggle on the settings page
Dark mode for the app's main screens
non_goals: The email templates and the printable invoice view, until open questions 1 and 2 are answered

criteria.text: Given the user switches the toggle on, when any main screen is opened, then the screen shows dark mode and the choice is kept after reload
criteria.check: End-to-end test over each main screen, with reload.

criteria.text: Given the toggle is off, when any main screen is opened, then the screen shows light mode
criteria.check: End-to-end test over each main screen.

expected_areas: Shared styling of the app's screens

open_questions.question: Do the email templates follow the toggle?

options.changes: Matches the non-goal; no criteria for emails
Adds criteria; email clients may override colours, which needs a test plan

open_questions.question: Does the printable invoice view follow the toggle?

options.option: No, it stays light for printing
options.changes: Matches the non-goal; no criteria for the invoice
Adds criteria for the invoice on screen and in print

open_questions.question: Is the choice per device or per account?

options.changes: Criterion 1 is checked across two sessions of one user; same storage question as the settings-across-devices spec
Criterion 1 is checked on one device only

actions_now: Writes a draft spec for the app screens and the toggle, leaves the email templates and invoice view out until the owner answers, and asks the owner about per-device versus per-account storage.
No spec is written: the request already states numbered criteria with checks, so the product role's contract does not apply. The request goes to implementation as it stands.

No spec is written: the cause is known and the expected behaviour is the page's existing one for users with an avatar, so this is a bug fix. The request goes to implementation, which should show the same page without the image for users with no avatar.

specs.title: Colleagues' last-online time
sources: Request from a team lead, passed on by the owner without comment
Binding: privacy decisions belong to a person
in_scope: Showing each user the last-online time of their colleagues
non_goals: Any display of this information until the privacy questions are answered

open_questions.question: Who may see a user's last-online time?

options.changes: Broadest exposure; needs an org-wide visibility criterion

options.option: Only members of the same team
options.changes: Needs team membership data in the check

options.option: Only users who opt in to share it
options.changes: Needs an opt-in setting and a criterion that hidden times are not shown

open_questions.question: Can a user hide their own last-online time?

options.option: Yes, with a visible off switch
options.changes: Adds a criterion for the switch and for hidden times
No hiding criterion; needs the owner's reason on record

open_questions.question: How long is last-online data kept?

options.option: A stated number of days, then deleted
options.changes: Adds a retention criterion with that number
No retention criterion; needs the owner's decision on record

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version, draft. No criteria are written until the owner decides who may see the data, whether it can be hidden and how long it is kept.

actions_now: Writes a draft with no criteria and three privacy questions for the owner, and escalates the decision: it is a privacy decision the product role does not make, so the feature does not proceed until the owner answers.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec CSV export version 2, approved (dl-015)
QA report: the spec does not say what happens above 100,000 rows; the current code times out
in_scope: The behaviour of an export above the row limit
non_goals: Changes to the reports page's columns or filter

criteria.text: Given an export would contain more rows than the limit in open question 1, when the user requests it, then the behaviour chosen in open question 1 applies and the user is told which rows were or were not exported
criteria.check: Integration test at 100,001 rows, once the owner has chosen the option.

open_questions.question: What happens when an export would have more than 100,000 rows?

options.option: Refuse with a message asking the user to narrow the date range
options.changes: No partial file; users must narrow the filter

options.option: Produce the file in the background and notify the user when it is ready
options.changes: Needs a notification and download step; a larger change

options.option: Export the first 100,000 rows with a clear notice
options.changes: Users get a file sooner; reconciliation must account for the truncation

versions: 3 (2026-11-27): adds criterion 5 and the row-limit question. Criteria 1 to 4 are unchanged from version 2. Draft until the owner approves version 3; version 2 is not edited in place.

actions_now: Issues version 3 as a draft that adds criterion 5 and the row-limit question, leaves version 2 unchanged, and asks the owner in chat to choose one of the three options. The implementer may continue with criteria 1 to 4.

specs.title: CSV export on the reports page
sources: Owner request: add CSV export to the reports page
Planned line: csv-export branch, separate from the partner API line

non_goals: The partner API, which has its own spec on its own branch

criteria.check: Integration test with a fixture report.

open_questions.question: Does the export contain only the filtered rows, or all rows?

options.changes: Criterion 1 applies to the filtered rows

specs.title: Partner REST API for reports
sources: Owner request: a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports
Decision dl-009: personal emails never leave the system in any export
in_scope: Read access for partners to the same reports as the reports page
non_goals: Changes to the reports page or to CSV export

criteria.text: Given a partner with a valid credential, when it requests a report, then it receives the same rows and columns the reports page shows for that report, without personal emails
criteria.check: Contract test comparing the API response with the page's data for a fixture report.

criteria.text: Given a request with no or an invalid credential, when it is sent, then it is refused and no report data is returned
criteria.check: Negative test.

criteria.text: Given a partner whose credential does not cover a report, when it requests that report, then it is refused and no report data is returned
criteria.check: Negative test.

open_questions.question: Who are the partners, and how do they get credentials?

options.option: API keys issued by the owner to named partners
options.changes: Criteria 2 and 3 rely on key scopes
Needs sign-up, consent and revocation criteria; a larger line

open_questions.question: Which reports and which fields are exposed?

options.option: The same reports as the page, minus personal emails
options.changes: Criterion 1 as written
Criterion 1 is narrowed by a named list

open_questions.question: What limits apply to partner requests?

No rate criterion; needs the owner's decision on record

specs.title: Report export for reconciliation
sources: Owner request: exports must contain every column of the report, so finance can reconcile
Decision dl-009: personal emails never leave the system in any export
in_scope: Every column of the report in the export, except the customer email column
non_goals: Sending customer email addresses in any export, which dl-009 forbids

criteria.text: Given a report export, when it is generated, then it contains every column of the report except Customer email, in the report's order
criteria.check: Test comparing the export's header with the report's column list minus Customer email.

criteria.text: Given a report with customer emails, when it is exported, then no personal email address appears anywhere in the file
criteria.check: Negative test scanning the exported file for email patterns.

open_questions.question: How does finance reconcile without the customer email column?

options.option: Export a customer identifier finance can match, if the owner confirms it is not personal data
options.changes: Adds a column and a criterion; needs the owner's decision

options.option: Finance gets the matching data through another route outside the export
options.changes: No new column; the route is outside this spec

options.option: The owner reopens dl-009 for finance exports
options.changes: Criterion 2 would change; only the owner can make this decision

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version, draft. The request conflicts with dl-009; the spec follows dl-009 and the conflict goes to the owner.

actions_now: Writes a draft that follows the recorded decision dl-009 and leaves out the customer email column, and escalates the contradiction with the request to the owner. The product role does not override dl-009.
